projects.title: Agentic Cybersecurity SOC
projects.tagline: Multi-agent Security Operations Center that triages logs and writes the incident report for you.
projects.description: A multi-agent SOC framework where specialised agents divide the incident-response workflow between them: one triages raw logs, one detects anomalies, one correlates findings against MITRE ATT&CK techniques, one drafts a mitigation plan, and a final agent assembles a human-readable incident report. Agents communicate through shared state, so a low-confidence result upstream forces a re-check downstream instead of silently propagating.
projects.problem: Security analysts drown in alert volume. Most alerts are noise, but the cost of missing the real one is asymmetric — so everything gets read, and analysts burn out on triage instead of investigation.
projects.approach: Split the analyst workflow into discrete agent roles with explicit hand-offs, ground every classification in MITRE ATT&CK, and require each agent to cite the log lines that justified its conclusion.
features: Log triage agent that clusters and prioritises raw events before any LLM reasoning happens
Statistical and model-based anomaly detection over event streams
Automatic MITRE ATT&CK technique correlation with confidence scoring
Mitigation planning agent that proposes ordered containment steps
Incident report generation in analyst-ready Markdown
Evidence citation — every claim links back to its source log lines

architecture.detail: Log normalisation and enrichment into a common event schema
Clustering and priority scoring to cut volume before LLM cost is incurred
Anomaly detection against behavioural baselines
MITRE ATT&CK mapping with confidence thresholds
Mitigation planning and incident report synthesis

projects.title: Self-Healing RAG
projects.tagline: A LangGraph RAG pipeline that notices when it is about to hallucinate and retries instead.
projects.description: An agentic retrieval-augmented generation pipeline built on LangGraph that treats the naive retrieve-then-generate loop as a starting point rather than the whole system. Before returning an answer it validates that every claim is grounded in retrieved context. If grounding fails it reformulates the query, retrieves again, and only surfaces an answer once the groundedness check passes — or explicitly says it does not know.
projects.problem: Standard RAG fails silently. When retrieval returns weak context the model still produces a fluent, confident, wrong answer, and nothing in the pipeline notices.
projects.approach: Model retrieval as a cyclic graph with validation nodes. Grounding, relevance and hallucination checks become first-class states with their own retry edges, so failure is recoverable instead of terminal.
features: Answer-grounding validation against retrieved evidence before response
Hallucination detection node with configurable strictness
Automatic query reformulation when retrieval quality is insufficient
Bounded retrieval retries to prevent infinite correction loops
Explicit abstention path — the system can say 'not in the corpus'
Per-node tracing so every retry decision is auditable

architecture.detail: Hybrid dense and sparse retrieval over the document corpus
Relevance scoring of each retrieved chunk against the question
Answer synthesis constrained to graded context
Groundedness and hallucination checks with retry edges
Query reformulation node that feeds back into retrieval

projects.title: LLM Guardrails Gateway
projects.tagline: A middleware layer that sits between your app and the model, and enforces the rules.
projects.description: A lightweight framework for securing and governing LLM applications. It intercepts requests on the way in and responses on the way out, applying prompt validation, content filtering, policy enforcement and response inspection — with observability hooks so you can see what was blocked and why. Designed to drop in as middleware rather than be rewritten into every call site.
projects.problem: Safety logic gets scattered across every LLM call site, implemented slightly differently each time, and becomes impossible to audit or update centrally.
projects.approach: Centralise the policy layer as a gateway. One place defines what is allowed in and out, one place emits the telemetry, and application code just makes calls.
features: Inbound prompt validation with injection-pattern detection
Configurable content filtering and PII redaction
Declarative policy enforcement independent of application code
Outbound response inspection before content reaches the user
Pluggable middleware chain — add checks without touching the core
Structured observability: what was blocked, by which rule, at what cost

architecture.detail: Prompt validation, injection detection and PII redaction
Declarative rule evaluation with allow, warn and block outcomes
Provider-agnostic dispatch to OpenAI, Anthropic, Groq or Ollama
Response inspection, toxicity and policy-compliance scoring
Structured logs and metrics for every decision

projects.title: LLM EvalForge
projects.tagline: Quality gates for LLM apps that fail the build, not the user.
projects.description: An automated quality-gate framework for LLM applications that runs as part of CI/CD. Every pull request triggers a benchmark suite covering hallucination, toxicity and policy compliance; results are published to GitHub Pages as a browsable report, and regressions below the configured threshold fail the build the same way a broken unit test would.
projects.problem: LLM behaviour regresses invisibly. A prompt tweak or model version bump can quietly degrade quality, and without automated evaluation nobody finds out until users complain.
projects.approach: Treat evaluation as testing. Define a benchmark suite, run it on every commit, publish the diff, and block merges when scores drop below threshold.
features: Automated hallucination, toxicity and policy-compliance scoring
Configurable AI guardrails per evaluation run
Reusable validation pipeline supporting multiple LLM providers
CI/CD integration with pass/fail thresholds that gate merges
GitHub Pages reporting with run-over-run comparison
Benchmark versioning so results stay comparable over time

architecture.detail: YAML-declared test cases, rubrics and thresholds
Provider-agnostic execution across the models under test
Hallucination, toxicity and compliance metric implementations
Threshold evaluation that returns a CI exit code
Static HTML report published to GitHub Pages

projects.title: InsightFlow AI
projects.tagline: Streaming ELT with fraud detection and LLM-generated insight on top.
projects.description: A production-style ELT architecture that takes an event stream from ingestion through feature engineering to a fraud-detection model, then layers OpenAI-generated narrative insight on top of the numbers. FastAPI serves the models, Streamlit renders the operator dashboard, and observability tooling tracks both pipeline health and model behaviour.
projects.problem: Analytics dashboards show what happened but not what it means. Meanwhile the fraud model and the data pipeline are usually two disconnected systems with no shared observability.
projects.approach: Build one pipeline where streaming ingestion, feature engineering, scoring and explanation are stages of the same system, with a single observability surface across all of them.

Reusable feature-engineering layer shared between training and serving
Fraud detection scoring exposed as a FastAPI service
LLM-generated narrative insight over aggregated metrics

Pipeline and model observability in one place

projects.title: AI Blood Group Prediction
projects.tagline: Full-stack fingerprint classification with ensemble deep learning and Grad-CAM explanations.
projects.description: A production-ready full-stack AI platform for fingerprint image classification. An ensemble of deep learning models produces the prediction, Grad-CAM produces the explanation, and the surrounding platform — JWT auth, analytics dashboard, multilingual UI, Redis caching, CI/CD — makes it something you could actually deploy rather than a notebook with a demo cell.
projects.problem: Most computer-vision projects stop at model accuracy. Nothing around the model — auth, caching, explanations, deployment — exists, so the result cannot be used by anyone but its author.
projects.approach: Build the whole system: React frontend, FastAPI backend, PostgreSQL and Redis, containerised, with explainability treated as a product feature rather than a debugging tool.

Grad-CAM heatmaps surfaced directly in the interface
JWT authentication with role-aware access

Multilingual interface support
Fully containerised with CI/CD pipelines

projects.title: AutoMail Agent
projects.tagline: An autonomous inbox assistant built on Claude that drafts, triages and files.
projects.description: A production-ready autonomous email assistant built with Claude, FastAPI and Streamlit. It classifies incoming mail by intent and urgency, drafts contextual replies, and keeps a human in the loop for anything it is not confident about — the approval step is a design decision, not a limitation.
projects.problem: Inbox triage is repetitive but not trivially automatable: the cost of a wrong autonomous reply is much higher than the cost of a slow one.
projects.approach: Let the agent do classification and drafting at full speed, but gate sending behind a confidence threshold and an explicit human approval surface.

Thread summarisation for long conversations

projects.title: AI Data Quality Monitoring
projects.tagline: Drift, anomalies and validation alerts for the datasets your models depend on.
projects.description: An end-to-end data quality monitoring system combining anomaly detection, drift monitoring and rule-based validation, wired to alerting and orchestrated with Airflow. MLflow tracks the monitoring models themselves, and a Streamlit dashboard makes the current health of every dataset legible at a glance.

projects.approach: Monitor the data as rigorously as the model: statistical drift detection, schema validation and anomaly scoring running on a schedule with real alerting.

Rule-based schema and constraint validation
Anomaly detection over data distributions

projects.title: GenAI Pipelines
projects.tagline: Five production-style GenAI pipelines, built end to end and documented to learn from.
projects.description: A teaching repository that builds five production-style GenAI pipelines from scratch: classical RAG, a legal-document AI, autonomous research agents, multimodal RAG over images and text, and an agentic system working against live data. Each pipeline is a complete, runnable system with its own trade-off discussion rather than a tutorial snippet.
projects.problem: GenAI tutorials teach the happy path. They skip chunking strategy, retrieval evaluation, cost control and the failure modes that actually determine whether a pipeline works.
projects.approach: Build five real pipelines with different constraints, and document what broke and why in each one.
features: Pipeline 1 — foundational RAG with chunking and retrieval evaluation
Pipeline 2 — legal AI with citation-grounded answers
Pipeline 3 — autonomous research agents with tool use
Pipeline 4 — multimodal RAG across text and images
Pipeline 5 — agentic AI operating on live external data
Cost and latency notes for each architecture

architecture.detail: Chunking, embedding and retrieval evaluation baselines
Legal document grounding with mandatory citation

projects.title: Project NEO

projects.approach: Combine wake-word detection, a persistent memory store and a tool-calling loop with real system-level actions behind a confirmation layer.

Persistent long-term memory across sessions

projects.title: NeuroQ — Quantum EEG Seizure Detection
projects.tagline: Quantum machine learning applied to EEG-based epilepsy diagnosis.
projects.description: An end-to-end EEG-based epilepsy diagnosis platform combining quantum machine learning, deep learning and classical signal processing for seizure classification. The pipeline runs from raw multi-channel EEG through filtering and feature extraction to a hybrid quantum-classical classifier, with the classical deep learning baseline retained for honest comparison.
projects.problem: EEG seizure detection is a high-dimensional, low-sample-count problem — exactly the regime where quantum feature maps are theorised to help, and where that claim is rarely tested against a fair baseline.
projects.approach: Build both models on the same preprocessing pipeline and evaluation protocol so the quantum variant is compared against a real deep learning baseline rather than a strawman.

Time and frequency-domain feature extraction
Hybrid quantum-classical classification circuit
Classical deep learning baseline on identical splits
Per-class evaluation with sensitivity and specificity reporting
Reproducible experiment configuration

architecture.detail: Filtering, segmentation and artefact rejection

projects.problem: Trip planning spans a dozen tools and a hundred small decisions, and single-prompt LLM answers produce itineraries that do not survive a budget check.
projects.approach: Decompose planning into specialised agents over shared state, so constraints propagate instead of being re-stated in every prompt.

projects.title: Meeting Intelligence

projects.approach: Extract to a strict schema — owner, action, decision, rationale, deadline — and validate before returning, so downstream tools can consume the result directly.

Decision log with captured rationale

projects.title: Tesla Stock Intelligence

projects.title: VisionSummoner

projects.description: A real-time gesture-based character summoning system using computer vision and hand tracking. Recognised gestures trigger animated overlays composited onto the live camera feed — a genuinely fun project that is also a serious exercise in low-latency CV pipelines.
projects.problem: Gesture interfaces feel broken the moment latency exceeds roughly 100ms, which rules out most naive per-frame inference designs.
projects.approach: Track landmarks rather than classify raw frames, debounce gesture state transitions, and keep the render loop decoupled from inference.
